transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (NovaFinance Head of ML), Tom Richards (Platform), Priya Patel (Security), Leo (PM)

Summary: Quick Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and prefix / KV cache recommendations for NovaFinance production mix (session-based chat + embeddings lookups). Covered tradeoffs (latency vs cost), dedicated vs hosted, basic cost model assumptions, and next steps for pilot benchmarking.

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, um yeah, quick roll call, um I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood, and with me is Daniel who will drive the technical walkthrough.
[00:12] Daniel Cho: hi all, Daniel Cho, solutions engineer. we'll go through Optimize (batching + caching), show the cost model, and then answer questions; feel free to interrupt.
[00:20] Aisha Khan: Hey, Aisha here. We own the ML infra side at NovaFinance. Looking forward — main thing is we need to get model latency under 220ms p95 for chat while keeping token cost within our budget.
[00:30] Tom Richards: Tom, platform eng. We're responsible for infra constraints — VPC, private subnets, egress controls, and cost attribution.
[00:36] Priya Patel: Priya, security. I'll ask the usual SSO/KMS/audit questions.
[00:40] Sofia: Great, thank you. Quick agenda: 1) brief qualification (current stack and traffic), 2) walkthrough of batching and KV/prefix cache recommendations, 3) cost modeling and tradeoffs, 4) Q&A and next steps.

--- Qualification / context (00:45 - 08:30) ---
[00:45] Daniel: Aisha, can you remind us of current traffic profile (qps, average seq len, embeddings calls)?
[00:50] Aisha: Sure. For our customer service assistant and risk assistant combined, steady-state is 40 qps, peaks at ~130 qps. Average prompt + response tokens ~450 tokens, but many sessions have short turns (~40-80 tokens). Embeddings are called for about 20% of sessions, batch size for embedding ingestion is done offline.
[01:20] Daniel: OK so a mix of long-tail sessions and short-turn chat — that actually benefits from prefix/KV caching because repeated system prompts and longer contexts show up. What's your current deployment?
[01:32] Tom: We're on a hybrid: some models run in-cloud with managed endpoints, other model infra is self-hosted on GCP VMs behind a private VPC. We prefer private deploys for sensitive queries, but we can use hosted endpoints for redacted traffic.
[01:48] Sofia: timeline and success criteria?
[01:52] Aisha: We want a pilot within 2-3 weeks, and if latency/cost numbers look good, move to a Dedicated contract by end of quarter. Success = <=220ms p95 chat for top flows and >=30% token cost reduction vs our baseline.

--- Walkthrough: Batching fundamentals (08:40 - 22:00) ---
[08:40] Daniel: Alright, quick slide — batching reduces per-token cost by combining requests into one GPU pass. Two levers: request batching (waiting a few ms to accumulate) and intra-request packing (multiple sequences in a batch). There is a latency vs throughput tradeoff: larger batches lower cost but add queuing latency.
[09:12] Aisha: what's the typical batching window you recommend for low-latency chat?
[09:16] Daniel: For chat with p95 < 220ms we typically recommend a short batching window, 3-6ms, and dynamic batch sizing that scales with QPS. We also use continuous batching on the runtime so cold-start is minimized. Note: the Optimize console will suggest batching policy based on your traffic profile.
[09:43] Tom: do you do request hedging or early returns if one token takes long?
[09:47] Daniel: We have per-token SLOs and can route to lower-cost model variants as fallback; for hedging we prefer routing policies rather than duplicative hedging.

--- Walkthrough: KV / prefix cache (22:10 - 36:00) ---
[22:10] Daniel: Next is prefix / KV cache. For Nova's use case, where system prompts and conversation prefixes repeat a lot (templates, policy context), prefix caching drastically reduces compute. The KV cache holds keys for recent contexts and reuses the cached KV for subsequent tokens, saving forward pass cost.
[22:40] Aisha: we've seen repeated system prompt + few-shot examples across sessions — that sounds promising. How big is the cache we should expect?
[22:52] Daniel: depends. For session-based chat where prefixes are ~300 tokens and repeat rate is ~40% across active users, you can expect 30-50% fewer forward passes. In practice we tune cache TTL and key granularity — exact hit rate depends on templating and personalization.
[23:25] Sofia: quick note — some customers call it "prefix cache" others call it "KV cache"; the runtime supports both and exposes metrics.
[23:35] Priya: what's stored in the cache — any PII or customer data concerns?
[23:40] Daniel: Great question. The cache stores model KV internal states (not raw user messages) but you should treat them as sensitive: in Private deployments the KV store stays in-customer VPC; in Hosted we encrypt at rest and you can use your KMS. We log hits/misses but don't retain raw payloads beyond configured retention.
[24:05] Priya: So for compliance we need KMS + audit logs and the ability to purge keys; is that available?
[24:12] Sofia: yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and we surface audit logs for cache access. We'll share the SOC2/KMS doc after the call.

--- Cost model example (36:10 - 47:00) ---
[36:10] Daniel: Now to the cost model. I'll run a quick example baseline vs optimized. Baseline: no KV cache, small batching (2-3), running on hosted endpoints with avg tokens per session 450. Baseline token cost estimate: $0.045 per 1k tokens (example) -> your monthly bill estimate $XXk (we used your anonymized mix). Optimized: batching window 4ms, dynamic batching to raise avg batch size by ~2x, prefix KV cache with 40% hit rate -> token compute drops ~35%, effective cost down to $0.029 per 1k. That's ~30-40% savings in unit compute.
[37:05] Aisha: those numbers look aligned with what we need — are those assuming quantized models or standard fp16?
[37:12] Daniel: Good catch — numbers assume 4-bit quantized model variants you can run on Dedicated instances. Hosted has mixed variants; we can route to quantized variants for non-production. Quantization typically gives a 1.6-2x inference throughput uplift and lowers cost assumptions.
[37:40] Tom: will quantization change latency jitter? We care about p95 consistency.
[37:45] Daniel: There's a small variance; on some workloads 4-bit quantized kernels are slightly faster per-token but may increase variability. Our runtime picks kernels to keep p95 stable; Optimize can reject a quantized variant if it worsens p95 beyond a threshold.
[38:05] Priya: Any effect on output quality? We can't compromise on regulatory responses.
[38:10] Daniel: We recommend an evaluation harness. Redwood Optimize integrates with evals — you can run prompt sets and compare quality metrics. In our pilots we saw negligible quality regression on standard few-shot chat with the recommended quantization profile.
[38:30] Aisha: ok. For the pilot can you produce per-route cost and latency estimates? We need to map product flows to cost centers.
[38:38] Daniel: Yes — we'll share a per-route spreadsheet; we already have a template that maps qps, tokens, batching policy, cache hit rate to monthly cost.

--- Objections & tradeoffs (47:10 - 50:30) ---
[47:10] Tom: one blocker is networking — we need to ensure egress policies and VPC peering for Private. How long to stand up a Private control plane?
[47:18] Sofia: Private deployment typically takes 3-6 weeks depending on approvals and network coordination; Dedicated (hosted dedicated) is faster for capacity-only needs. We'll work with your infra team.
[47:28] Aisha: Another concern: cache cold start when user base spikes — does Optimize pre-warm anything?
[47:33] Daniel: We offer pre-warming and intelligent TTL policies; Optimize can prime the cache for expected prefixes (e.g., top system prompts) during ramp.
[47:45] Priya: last security Q: can we audit who accessed cached entries and when?
[47:50] Daniel: Yes audit logs include cache ops; in Private these feed to your SIEM.

--- Recap & next steps (50:40 - 52:00) ---
[50:40] Sofia: quick recap — Daniel will produce the latency/cost estimate using your sample traffic, I'll send pricing and Private deployment checklist / SOC2 + KMS docs, and we'll schedule a pilot benchmark week of 8/17.
[50:55] Aisha: sounds good. Action items?
[50:58] Sofia: I'll capture and email after the call. Any final Qs?
[51:05] Tom: none from me.
[51:07] Priya: none.
[51:09] Aisha: thanks everyone.
[51:12] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up.
